newsitem.title: UK: GEC unit wins oiler order from UK navy.
newsitem.headline: GEC unit wins oiler order from UK navy.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday it had awarded a 200 million pound contract for two auxiliary oiler ships to Barrow-based VSEL, a unit of GEC Marine.
VSEL had been invited in February 1996 to tender for the contract along with Kvaerner Govan Ltd, owned by the Norwegian industrial group Kvaerner ASA.

The two fast fleet tankers, which will be used to replenish warships at sea with fuel, lubricants and some solid stores, are expected to enter service early in the next century, defence procurement minister James Arbuthnot told parliament.
He said in a written answer VSEL had won the contract because it would provide the best value for money for the taxpayer.

The two oilers will displace 27,000 tons, have a speed of 18 knots and a range of 8,000 miles. The vessels will meet the latest marine safety standards, with double hulls to protect against pollution. They also have a helicopter flight deck.
The order will sustain about 900 jobs at VSEL and its sub-contractors, Arbuthnot said.
Kvaerner had warned that it might have to close the Govan yard near Glasgow, which it took over in 1988, if it lost the order. More than 1,000 jobs could be at risk.
